why_use_this: Reach for this package the moment a computation needs \( i = \sqrt{-1} \) -- roots of a negative discriminant, AC circuit analysis, Fourier/frequency-domain work (see [vani-signal](https://github.com/enthusiasticgeek/vani-signal), which depends on this package for exactly that), or anywhere a real-only type like `f64` simply can't represent the answer. `Complex` is a plain `{ re: f64, im: f64 }` struct with no heap-owning fields, so it's freely copyable -- every function here takes and returns `Complex` by value, no `ref`/`mut ref` ceremony anywhere, unlike the `Vec<f64>`-based sibling libraries. If your problem never leaves the reals (no square roots of negative numbers, no oscillating phase/frequency content), you don't need this package at all -- reach for it specifically when a real number stops being enough.

math_notes.complex_conj: \( \bar{z} = a - bi \) for \( z = a + bi \) -- negates the imaginary part only.
math_notes.complex_neg: \( -z = -a - bi \) for \( z = a + bi \) -- negates both parts.
math_notes.complex_mul: \( (a+bi)(c+di) = (ac - bd) + (ad + bc)i \), the standard FOIL expansion using \( i^2 = -1 \).
math_notes.complex_norm_sq: \( |z|^2 = a^2 + b^2 \) for \( z = a+bi \) -- avoids the square root `complex_abs` needs, useful whenever only a comparison or a denominator (as in `complex_div`/`complex_reciprocal`) is needed.
math_notes.complex_div: \( \dfrac{a+bi}{c+di} = \dfrac{(a+bi)(c-di)}{c^2+d^2} = \dfrac{ac+bd}{c^2+d^2} + \dfrac{bc-ad}{c^2+d^2}i \) -- multiply through by the denominator's conjugate to clear the imaginary part from the denominator, then divide by \( |c+di|^2 \) (`complex_norm_sq`).
math_notes.complex_scale: \( s \cdot (a+bi) = sa + sbi \) -- real scalar multiplication, componentwise.
math_notes.complex_reciprocal: \( \dfrac{1}{z} = \dfrac{\bar{z}}{|z|^2} = \dfrac{a}{a^2+b^2} - \dfrac{b}{a^2+b^2}i \) for \( z = a+bi \neq 0 \) -- the \( n=-1 \) special case of `complex_div`, conjugate over norm-squared.
math_notes.complex_abs: \( |z| = \sqrt{a^2+b^2} = r \) -- the modulus, i.e. the distance from the origin in the complex plane; the \( r \) of \( z \)'s polar form \( r e^{i\theta} \).
math_notes.complex_arg: \( \arg(z) = \operatorname{atan2}(b, a) \in (-\pi, \pi] \) -- the angle from the positive real axis; the \( \theta \) of \( z \)'s polar form \( r e^{i\theta} \).
math_notes.complex_from_polar: \( z = r(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta) = re^{i\theta} \) -- the inverse of the (`complex_abs`, `complex_arg`) pair: rebuilds Cartesian \( (a,b) \) from polar \( (r,\theta) \).
math_notes.complex_exp: \( e^{a+bi} = e^a(\cos b + i\sin b) \) -- Euler's formula, the reason a complex exponential just scales-and-rotates rather than needing anything more exotic than real `exp`/`sin`/`cos`.
math_notes.complex_log: \( \log z = \ln|z| + i\arg(z) \) -- the principal branch of the complex logarithm (imaginary part restricted to \( (-\pi, \pi] \) via `complex_arg`'s own range), the inverse of `complex_exp` on that branch.
math_notes.complex_pow_i64: \( z^n \) for integer \( n \), via repeated `complex_mul` for \( n > 0 \) (and `complex_reciprocal` of \( z^{|n|} \) for \( n < 0 \)) -- not De Moivre's polar-form formula \( r^n(\cos n\theta + i \sin n\theta) \), though the two agree mathematically.
math_notes.complex_sqrt: \( \sqrt{z} = \sqrt{r}\, e^{i\theta/2} \) -- the principal square root, computed via the polar form (`complex_abs`/`complex_arg` then `complex_from_polar` with the halved angle and square-rooted modulus), always returning the root with non-negative real part.
math_notes.complex_sin: \( \sin(a+bi) = \sin a \cosh b + i \cos a \sinh b \) -- the complex sine, unbounded in magnitude (unlike real `sin`) because of the `cosh`/`sinh` growth in the imaginary direction.
math_notes.complex_tan: \( \tan z = \sin z / \cos z \), computed from `complex_sin`/`complex_cos` via `complex_div` -- not a separate closed form.
math_notes.complex_tanh: \( \tanh z = \sinh z / \cosh z \), computed from `complex_sinh`/`complex_cosh` via `complex_div`.
math_notes.complex_nth_roots_of_unity: The \( n \) solutions to \( z^n = 1 \): \( z_k = e^{2\pi i k / n} = \cos\!\left(\dfrac{2\pi k}{n}\right) + i\sin\!\left(\dfrac{2\pi k}{n}\right) \) for \( k = 0, 1, \ldots, n-1 \), each built via `complex_from_polar` with radius 1.
